title: function_to_go council pipeline: un-run detection, cost quote, approval gate, chunked run, clearinghouse publish
confront: ran: task-d9e8311c, codex researcher on h100, 12 binding stalls returned, 9 folded, 0 dropped
review_protocol: Written single-pass in Draft Mode: every judgement call is decided in the body and manifested in '## Open Questions and Judgement Calls' (Q1-Q14), ordered by blast radius descending. Chris edits the committed fullprompt.md in place, annotating with (CSH ...) markers; `/ai-miles d --review function-to-go-council-pipeline-v1` then diffs the working tree against draft_commit, classifies every hunk, propagates decision changes through the body, user stories, testing decisions, gotchas and taskplan.json, and recommits with a fresh baseline. The PRD is held at draft until one review round completes (review_rounds >= 1), which is the hard ready gate.
stages: 3 human approval bound to quote_hash, with a token ceiling -> APPROVED.json
4 chunked run with a retry pass and an account-wide pacer -> RUN.json
5 export parquet, shard, publish; kbhub loads and verifies -> shard/ + LOADED.json
findings: Four of the five stages already exist in KBUtilLib; the 2026-10-20 hand-driven run bypassed all of them, and every defect it hit is a consequence of the bypass rather than a missing capability.

RESOLVED THIS SESSION: the 760 'never submitted' definitions flagged as an unexplained coverage gap are the retrieval stage's abstained rows. Measured against ranked.jsonl.gz and priority_adp1_pmi.tsv: 20,036 distinct definitions = 19,276 non-abstained (exactly what was submitted) + 760 abstained, the two sets disjoint. Nothing is missing.
The clearinghouse is READABLE from h100 off-pod over the BERDL delta API (measured 2026-10-22, 16 successful queries). Only load and verify are in-pod. Stage 1 does not need kbhub.
function_result holds 0 rows: the 19,268 verdicts are not loaded. function_entity and function_content hold 47,341 rows each, which is exactly the row count of ranked.jsonl.gz.

ROUND 2, from Chris's review: the clearinghouse parameter_set must be keyed on a model-only bench_fingerprint, NOT Roster.fingerprint(). Measured at types.py:507, Roster.fingerprint covers role, endpoint_kind, model (route spelling), canonical_model, max_output_tokens, temperature and extra -- so it includes the TRANSPORT, and a codex->MAG move would have re-partitioned all 47,341 clearinghouse functions and re-charged ~199M tokens for a pure cost optimisation. roster_fingerprint and route_fingerprint remain as provenance. prompt_hash deliberately KEEPS endpoint_kind (Q8): measured, the same ~1,400-token question cost ~63,000 input tokens over claude -p against 1,403 over the API, so CLI and API answers are not interchangeable.

<T>_result is keyed on parameter_set_hash and current_state() windows per parameter set, so 'un-run at THIS version' is a native query. The parameter set is where query_version, roster_fingerprint and mapping_hash belong.

prompt_hash is a PURE function (types.py:264) and seat_generation_params exists so a fingerprint can be computed without a backend, so the quote can be EXACT for proposer and critic with zero API calls, and reuse is one indexed lookup per prompt against ix_calls_prompt_hash_status.
The token model can be fitted from attempts.usage over the run's own 199.2M tokens, removing any third-party tokenizer dependency across a Google/OpenAI/Anthropic roster.

Neither ARGO nor MAG publishes a rate card (every usage/billing/pricing/quota path 404s; MAG /models/<id> returns 401 'only proxy admin'). Vendor list rates were solved exactly from the Claude CLI's costBasis=list, but a $350/month ARGO cap was exhausted in a week, so ARGO's effective multiple over list is unknown and >1. A list-derived dollar figure is a FLOOR.

kbu clearinghouse plan/shard/load/verify is a complete idempotent loader: declarative TOML manifest, bronze parquet, run.json with per-batch sha256 + row count + hash range, a five-check pre-use integrity gate, fill-only appends, a resumable ledger, --dry-run as 'the operator's last gate', and registry-before-results ordering. Nobody needs to write a kbhub loader.

FileSourceAdapter accepts exactly parquet | jsonl | tsv and _iter_jsonl uses a plain open(), so gzipped JSONL is NOT readable by the manifest path. Parquet is the answer: compressed, exact row count from the footer, and read_batch_table refuses anything else.

BLOCKER: commit 0825c5a ('readiness must accept every id a gateway advertises') exists in NO shared branch -- the object is not present in the Dropbox repo. It lives only in h100's editable install. Without it servable.py reads the gateway's display spelling while /chat/completions accepts only internal_id, so readiness is the exact inverse of the call: every ARGO seat is refused at submit and kbu council doctor reports the whole ARGO bench unavailable. Three of five seats are ARGO. The council on main cannot run.

completed_run.retry_recovery: 105 of 113 on one retry, for 0.30% of run cost

open_contingencies: ARGO's and MAG's effective token rates are derivable from no artifact; the design assumes an operator-supplied rate table plus a per-run balance delta, and reports 'unpriced' otherwise. This is the one flag-not-question in the PRD.
The granularity of ClearinghouseLockUnavailableError is unestablished, so whether two shard runs can load concurrently is unknown. Affects only whether pending runs must be loaded in series.

Whether endpoint_state's halt path actually STOPS a running worker on a budget overrun, as opposed to merely recording the halt, is unverified. t9 is instructed to verify and report. If it does not, Q6's ceiling mechanism changes.

Why the uncompressed JSONL had not reached kbhub while the sync client reported the directory up to date is unknown. The design routes around it via run.json plus per-batch sha256, but 'the sync client said up to date' is now established as not a completeness signal.

Whether `temperature` should be scientifically load-bearing. It is EXCLUDED from bench_fingerprint because it is substantially transport-coupled and including it would let a routing change re-partition the corpus through the back door. On a near-deterministic JSON-extraction task that is the right trade, but it is the one line in Q2 a reasonable person could reverse -- and if reversed it belongs in the QUERY VERSION, not the bench hash.
